title: HQML-ICU: hybrid quantum-classical machine learning for ICU mortality prediction using MIMIC-IV electronic health records
summary: In a retrospective single-center analysis of 38,624 MIMIC-IV ICU admissions, a hybrid quantum-classical model predicted in-hospital mortality with test AUROC 0.871 versus 0.858 for XGBoost (DeLong p=0.012), with the difference also reported in five-fold cross-validation. The quantum circuit ran in noiseless statevector simulation on classical hardware; external validation is needed.
ai_technology: A learned hybrid quantum-classical model (classical autoencoder, variational quantum circuit and classical output layer) predicts in-hospital mortality from first-day ICU data.
organization: University of Tehran; Sharif University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; publication date and first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: Test-set comparison and five-fold cross-validation on a single-center MIMIC-IV cohort; authors describe noiseless classical statevector simulation.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective single-center cohort; simulated quantum circuit on classical hardware and no external validation.
evidence.ai_role: A learned hybrid quantum-classical model (classical autoencoder, variational quantum circuit and classical output layer) predicts in-hospital mortality from first-day ICU data.
